subject: maths
promptStrong: Give me an exam-style {board} {level} {subject} question on {lo}, then mark my answer against the mark scheme.
promptWeak: Explain {lo} for {board} {level} {subject} simply, with a clear example and the most common mistake students make.

questions.q: What is the formula for the area of a circle of radius r?
questions.explain: The area of a circle is π multiplied by the radius squared.

questions.q: The circumference of a circle of diameter d is given by which formula?
questions.explain: Circumference equals π times the diameter (equivalently 2πr).

questions.q: What is the volume of a sphere of radius r?
questions.explain: The volume of a sphere is four-thirds π times the radius cubed.

questions.q: What is the volume of a cone with base radius r and height h?
questions.explain: A cone's volume is one-third of the volume of a cylinder with the same base and height.

questions.q: What is the area of a trapezium with parallel sides a and b and height h?
questions.explain: The area of a trapezium is half the sum of the parallel sides multiplied by the perpendicular height.

questions.q: What is the sum of the interior angles of a polygon with n sides?
questions.explain: A polygon can be split into (n − 2) triangles, each contributing 180°.

questions.q: Pythagoras' theorem for a right-angled triangle with hypotenuse c states that:
questions.explain: The square on the hypotenuse equals the sum of the squares on the other two sides.

questions.q: When a straight line crosses two parallel lines, alternate angles are:
questions.explain: Alternate angles (forming a Z-shape) between parallel lines are equal.

questions.q: The exterior angle of a triangle is equal to:
options: The sum of the two opposite interior angles
questions.explain: An exterior angle equals the sum of the two interior angles not adjacent to it.

questions.q: The perpendicular bisector of a line segment AB is the locus of points that are:
options: A fixed distance from the line AB
Closer to A than to B
questions.explain: Every point on the perpendicular bisector is the same distance from both endpoints.

questions.q: The bisector of an angle is the locus of points that are:
options: Equidistant from the two lines forming the angle
Equidistant from the two endpoints of a segment
A fixed distance from the vertex
On the perpendicular from the vertex
questions.explain: An angle bisector is the set of points the same perpendicular distance from both arms of the angle.

questions.q: How is the volume of any prism calculated?
questions.explain: A prism has a uniform cross-section, so its volume is that area multiplied by its length.

questions.q: Which relationship correctly links density, mass and volume?
questions.explain: Density is mass per unit volume, so it equals mass divided by volume.

questions.q: To add the column vectors (2, 3) and (4, 1), you should:
options: Add the corresponding components to get (6, 4)
Add all four numbers to get 10
questions.explain: Column vectors are added by summing their top components and their bottom components separately.

questions.q: If b = 3a, what is the relationship between vectors a and b?
options: b is parallel to a and three times its length
b is the reverse of a
b has the same length as a
questions.explain: Multiplying a vector by a positive scalar keeps its direction but scales its magnitude.

questions.q: In a circle, the angle subtended at the centre by an arc is:
options: Twice the angle subtended at the circumference
Equal to the angle at the circumference
Half the angle at the circumference
questions.explain: By the circle theorem, the angle at the centre is double the angle at the circumference from the same arc.

questions.q: What is the size of each interior angle of a regular hexagon?
questions.explain: Interior angle sum is (6 − 2) × 180° = 720°, and 720° ÷ 6 = 120°.

questions.q: A circle has radius 5 cm. What is its area, to 1 decimal place?
questions.explain: Area = π × 5² = 25π ≈ 78.5 cm².

questions.q: What is the magnitude of the vector (3, 4)?
questions.explain: Magnitude = √(3² + 4²) = √25 = 5.

questions.q: A right-angled triangle has the two shorter sides 6 cm and 8 cm. What is the length of the hypotenuse?
questions.explain: Using Pythagoras, √(6² + 8²) = √100 = 10 cm.
